name: South Oxfordshire

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme: the council says it does not run any additional or selective licensing schemes.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: HMOs with five or more people who are not all one household need a mandatory licence for five years. HMOs for more than six people also need planning permission.

neighbourhoods.name: Henley-on-Thames

neighbourhoods.name: Didcot
neighbourhoods.housing: A fast-growing town with Victorian terraces near the station and very large new-build areas such as Great Western Park.

neighbourhoods.name: Thame
neighbourhoods.housing: A market town with timber-framed and Georgian houses along its wide high street and newer estates around it.

neighbourhoods.name: Wallingford
neighbourhoods.housing: A historic Thames town of period houses and terraces, with post-war and new-build estates.

neighbourhoods.name: Berinsfield
neighbourhoods.housing: A post-war village of council-built houses, now partly let privately.

neighbourhoods.name: Wheatley
neighbourhoods.housing: A large village east of Oxford with stone cottages, post-war houses and newer infill.

neighbourhoods.name: Chinnor
neighbourhoods.housing: A village under the Chilterns with older cottages and large post-war and modern estates.

housing: South Oxfordshire is a largely rural district between Oxford, Reading and the Chilterns, with market towns at Henley, Thame, Wallingford and Didcot. Older homes are brick, flint and timber-framed cottages and Georgian town houses, and many villages are conservation areas; Didcot is the main growth town, with thousands of new-build homes. Private renting is below average and prices are among the highest in Oxfordshire. Science and research jobs at Culham and Harwell nearby bring demand for lets.
checkinTips: New-build homes in Didcot's new estates: photograph snagging items, sealant, paintwork and the garden, and note any estate management charge areas.
Brick and flint cottages in the Chilterns villages: photograph walls inside for damp, beams, low doorways and the condition of any wood burner.
Riverside homes in Henley, Wallingford and Goring: check ground floors, cellars and gardens for signs of past flooding from the Thames.
Rural homes off the gas grid: record the oil tank and gauge level or LPG tank, and any septic tank or treatment plant cover.
Larger detached houses: record the garden, hedges, gates, garages and outbuildings, and agree what upkeep the tenant is expected to do.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact South Oxfordshire District Council's Private Sector Housing Team (shared with the Vale of White Horse), which can inspect homes and take action against landlords.
